title: SYSK’s 2018 Super Spooktacular
summary: SYSK's annual ad-free Halloween episode, in which Josh and Chuck take turns reading spooky fiction with sound effects. First they read "Ancient Lights" by Algernon Blackwood, about a Croydon surveyor's clerk who wanders into a haunted wood, where the trees and figures seem to watch him and he escapes after being tangled in nettles and a trick gate. They then read Edgar Allan Poe's "Hop-Frog," in which a disabled court jester takes revenge on a cruel king and his seven ministers by dressing them as chained orangutans and setting them on fire with a torch under a hanging chandelier chain. The hosts discuss the authors' lives, Poe's death in Baltimore, the Jodie Foster film The Watcher in the Woods, and the listener poll on scariness. They close by wishing listeners a happy Halloween.

segments.title: Halloween opening and setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the annual ad-free Halloween episode, explain that they will read spooky stories themselves this year with Jerry's sound design, and set a spooky mood.

segments.title: Reading 'Ancient Lights' by Algernon Blackwood
segments.summary: Josh reads Algernon Blackwood's 'Ancient Lights', in which a Croydon surveyor's clerk walks through Sussex fields toward a red house, enters a wood with a trespassing sign, gets lost in a shifting, watchful forest with illusory figures, and finally escapes. The hosts comment on the story and mention The Watcher in the Woods.

segments.title: Discussion of Blackwood and the poll
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Algernon Blackwood, mistake him for Ambrose Bierce, mention The Empty House, and take a show of hands on who is scared.

segments.title: Introducing Poe and public domain rights
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Edgar Allan Poe's death in Baltimore, joke about buying rights to modern authors' work, and mention Joyce Carol Oates. They introduce 'Hop-Frog' as a public domain story.

segments.title: Reading 'Hop-Frog' by Edgar Allan Poe
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh read Poe's 'Hop-Frog': a cruel king and his seven ministers, a disabled jester and his friend Trippetta, a masquerade plot in which the jester dresses the king and ministers as chained orangutans, and a fiery revenge in which the jester and Trippetta escape through the skylight.

segments.title: Closing thoughts and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts react to the ending, suggest naming something after Hop-Frog and Trippetta, and wish listeners a happy and safe Halloween before promising a regular episode next time.
